requirements.requirement: Repair /srv/legacy2/numeric-record-ordering/bin/merge so the staged exports publish to merged.csv with one header, numeric transaction_id ordering, CSV-aware quoted fields, and identical-duplicate collapse.
requirements.summary: The repaired executable merged the default staged exports into the required location. Semantic verification directly observed one header, IDs ordered 2, 10, 100, preservation of “Tape, wide” as one field, and one retained row for duplicate ID 2. The same behavior passed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Conflicting duplicate transaction IDs must stop publication, explain the conflict, and leave the existing output intact.
requirements.summary: A conflicting ID 2 caused exit code 1, with a diagnostic identifying the ID, both source locations, and both differing records. The before and after merged.csv hashes were identical. This behavior also passed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 before and after execution/restart. The implementation used the already available /usr/bin/python3 and executed successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence, including successful publication, conflict rejection with atomic output preservation, platform retention, and persistence across the mandatory node restart. Operational hygiene was strong apart from two retained diagnostic files in /tmp.
limitations: Functional testing used the supplied staged exports and one deliberate conflict case; it did not exhaustively exercise every possible malformed CSV or numeric-ID edge case.
The fixed lifecycle collector inventories /tmp and broad system health but not the complete final /srv handover tree, so it cannot independently rule out unlisted incidental files there.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: replacing bin/merge, publishing the requested output, exercising atomic failure behavior, and performing the mandatory restart. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation, failed service, package damage, or new network exposure was observed. The only hygiene defect is retained diagnostic residue: /tmp/merge-conflict.out from cmd-647d00a9185b4d5a and /tmp/post-restart-conflict.out from cmd-af912c0cfb3b4b02 remained after execution instead of being removed. These are bounded, low-risk files. Restart-created systemd-private path and socket PID changes are normal reboot effects, not residue. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged restart, changed boot ID, running recovered state, persistent data, and successful post-restart functional checks, corroborated by fixed lifecycle identities.
